labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane/1-causality
labels.notes: #print Causal.oneWayMembrane gives le U := TransGen (membraneStep U), lt := False. membraneStep U a b is a <= b in the product order of R x R, segment R a b inside U, and (a in R -> b in R), with R = membraneRight = {p | p.2 < p.1}. In null coordinates (u, v) = (t + x1, t - x1), the closed future cone of 1+1 Minkowski space is the product order (Delta t >= |Delta x1| iff Delta u, Delta v >= 0), and v < u iff x1 > 0. So R = {x1 > 0} and L = {x1 <= 0} with the membrane in L, as the target says. Along a segment x1 is affine, so the per-step condition is exactly 'never passes from R into L'. Every field of the library structure Causal.Causality (Causal/Causality.lean:77) is discharged: le_mem by head'/tail', le_refl by the trivial segment, le_trans by TransGen.trans, le_mono by enlarging U, and the lt fields by False. Nothing is degenerate: le top is in closed form x <= y and (x in R -> y in R) (oneWayMembrane_le_top_iff). The polygonal reading is disclosed in the SCOPE and in the REPORT's questions. I re-derived the equivalence with continuous causal curves. Take an inscribed polygon on a fine partition: a thickening of the compact image lies in U and uniform continuity does the rest. The vertices are product-monotone, and the membrane condition passes to the vertices because the set of times spent in R is an up-set. The converse holds by affinity. So the two readings give the same le_U. The OQ-69 answer does not depend on this: it is existential, and the witness is the polygonal causality. See finding 3 on wording.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane/2-arc-connected
labels.notes: oneWayMembrane_causallyArcConnected states Causal.Causality.CausallyArcConnected, which is the ladder's lean (ladder.toml:252). The constants were read off the elaborated type. The curves are the membrane's own: CausalCurveOn is CurveOn C.le, and #print CurveOn has fields mem and rel. A step is realised by its affine curve: a ball in N, a preimage interval, convexity, and pos_affine_of_pos for the side. A chain is realised by CurveOn.exists_concat. The lt half holds because lt is False and no ChronalCurveOn exists, through the library's causallyArcConnectedOn_iff. oneWayMembrane_causallyArcConnectedOn W follows by mono.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane/3-absolutely-minimal
labels.notes: oneWayMembrane_absolutelyMinimal uses Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal (ladder.toml:246) and comes from CausallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimal (ArcConnected.lean:216). oneWayMembrane_absolutelyMinimalOn (W) uses Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimalOn. Its definition (Generated.lean:239): for every cover S of W and every open V <= W, every le_V and lt_V is a TransGen of relations in V inf O, O in S. So its universal closure is the either-reading form of kb/0074, OQ-18 and OQ-69. It implies the library node through Precausality.absolutelyMinimal_iff. The dual forms hold in the same way.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane/4-tarentin
labels.notes: oneWayMembrane_tarentin uses Causal.Causality.Tarentin (ladder.toml:264). #print: forall x, forall U in nhds x, exists p in U, exists q in U, x in openDiamond top p q. That is def:tarentin_spacetime (ETT.tex:677-680), quoted verbatim in the docstring. I checked the three cases by hand. On the membrane, p = x - (r/2, r/4) lies strictly in {u < v} and q = x + (r/2, r/4) lies in R, so the whole open box between them lies in J_M(p, q); J_M(p, q) is in fact the full order interval. In R, and in {u < v}, the box is cut to that side. Nit: the docstring's '(the planner's m -/+ (delta, 2 delta) in (x1, t))' is loose. The Lean's (2e, e) in null coordinates is (e/2, 3e/2) in (x1, t). The REPORT's 'same shape' is the accurate wording.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane/5-causally-open-future
labels.notes: oneWayMembrane_causallyOpenFuture uses Causal.Causality.CausallyOpenFuture (ladder.toml:240). #print: forall U V : Opens, V <= U -> IsOpen (Jplus U V). That is def:causally_open_spacetime_open as printed (ETT.tex:694-697), for every open U, not only U = top. The proof shifts the chain along -(eta, eta), which keeps x1 and so the side: each step goes through membraneStep.shift_sub, by a thickening of the compact segment inside U. Then one last step from y - (m, m) reaches a ball about y, on y's side when y is in R. The statement is not vacuous: J+_U(V) is a genuine cone set. LocallyCausallyOpenFuture (ladder.toml lean) follows by CausallyOpenFuture.locallyCausallyOpenFuture.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane/6-not-causally-open-past
labels.notes: The box (-1, 1) x (1, 3) in null coordinates is centred at (t, x1) = (1, -1) and lies inside {u < v}, so strictly left of the membrane. I re-derived oneWayMembrane_Jminus_box: a point of R never precedes a point of L, so J-_M(V) = {u <= v, u < 1, v < 3}. It contains (0, 0) and no (d, 0) with d > 0, so it is not open (oneWayMembrane_not_isOpen_Jminus_box). oneWayMembrane_not_causallyOpenPast states the negation of CausallyOpenFuture for oneWayMembrane.dual, which is definitionally 'forall U V, V <= U -> IsOpen (Jminus U V)'. oneWayMembrane_not_causallyOpen states the negation of Causal.Causality.CausallyOpen (ladder.toml:234, two-sided by DEC-8) through its second conjunct. A box rather than the sketch's small ball: one open V suffices.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane/7-local
labels.notes: oneWayMembrane_not_locallyCausallyOpen is the negation of Causal.Causality.LocallyCausallyOpen (ladder.toml:314). #print: LocallyCausallyOpenFuture C and LocallyCausallyOpenFuture C.dual. It is proved directly at (0, 0) through oneWayMembrane_not_causallyOpenPastOn: if m is in W and m.1 = m.2, then W is not causally open in the past. The witnesses are a box of L above m, inside W, and the point m + (rho/2, 0) of R, which cannot precede it. The sharp form, oneWayMembrane_causallyOpenPastOn_iff, says dual.CausallyOpenFutureOn W iff forall z in W, z.1 != z.2: an open set is causally open in the past iff it misses the membrane {x1 = 0}. The converse half is oneWayMembrane_Jminus_mem_nhds, for every U and V <= U <= W. Off the membrane each side is open, and the push along +(eta, eta) keeps the side. True as stated.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane/8-time-reversal
labels.notes: The dual is causally arc-connected, absolutely minimal (and On, for every W) and tarentin, through the library's dual_causallyArcConnectedOn and dual_tarentin, whose types I printed. It is not LocallyCausallyOpenFuture: proved directly at (0, 0), not through causal_ladder. Its time function is -(u + v), continuous and strictly increasing along dual.le top. Every other conjunct of oneWayMembrane_dual_separates goes through a library dual_* iff.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane/9-ladder
labels.notes: Each conclusion uses the ladder's constant: PushUp, LocallyPushUp, IsCausal, StronglyCausalOpen, StronglyCausal, HasTimeFunction, CurvesExtend, CausallyCompact, GloballyHyperbolic, CausallyPlain, ChronalNeighbours. Push-up is vacuous because lt is empty, which the REPORT discloses. Causal: le lies in the product order. StronglyCausalOpen: a sup-norm ball contains the order interval of any two of its points, and every diamond lies in Icc. Time function u + v. CurvesExtend through HasTimeFunction.curvesExtend. Not causally compact: (0, -1) and (2, 1) lie in R, so J_M between them is Icc cut to R, whose closure holds (0, 0); I re-derived this. Not GH, since GH implies causally compact. Not plain, since Int J+(M) = M while I+(M) is empty. No chronal neighbours, since lt is empty. Alexandrov topology = topology through StronglyCausal.alexandrovTopology_eq (type: Tarentin -> StronglyCausal -> alexandrovTopology = inst), so no causal openness is used, as the docstring says.

labels.label: T-abs-one-way-membrane/10-separation
labels.notes: From the elaborated types (getUsedConstants): oneWayMembrane_separates has exactly the 18 conjuncts the REPORT lists, each the ladder's lean. oneWayMembrane_dual_separates has the 18 listed for the dual, with the two future-openness conjuncts negated. exists_tarentin_absolutelyMinimal_causallyOpenFuture_not_past states: exists C : Causality (R x R), (forall W, C.AbsolutelyMinimalOn W), C.CausallyArcConnected, C.Tarentin, C.CausallyOpenFuture and not C.dual.CausallyOpenFuture. That is OQ-69's question (registers/DECISIONS.md:225) answered yes, in either reading. The space is R x R, which is T2 and second countable by mathlib instances, so it is one of ETT's topological spacetimes. The three _bare forms negate universal implications over Causality (R x R): AbsolutelyMinimal (or AbsolutelyMinimalOn for every W) with Tarentin and CausallyOpenFuture does not give CausallyOpen; CausallyArcConnected with Tarentin does not give LocallyCausallyOpenFuture. One instance refutes the general claim. On ETT.tex, I read the proof of prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality (:713-751). (i) is strong causality and (ii) is 'the Alexandrov topology is the topology'. The membrane meets the printed hypotheses (tarentin, and J+ open as printed at :694-697), and both (i) and (ii) hold in Lean (oneWayMembrane_stronglyCausalOpen, oneWayMembrane_alexandrovTopology_eq). So it is no counterexample, and the closer says so everywhere. Line 746 equates J+(int J+(a_i)) cap J-(int J-(b_i)) with int J+(a_i) cap int J-(b_i), justified at :741 by openness. Its J- factor fails at b = (1, 3) (oneWayMembrane_not_Jminus_interior_Jminus_subset): (0, 0) precedes the interior point (0, 1) and is not interior. I re-derived this. The chain's conclusion J(a, b) inside int J(a_i, b_i) fails for the single open diamond W = int J((-1, 0), (3, 4)), with a = (0, 1) and b = (2, 3), whose diamond holds the membrane point (1, 1) (oneWayMembrane_not_causallyConvexIn_openDiamond). That W is a legitimate choice at :739-740, and since :744-745 and :747 are valid, the intersection form of :746 also fails there. Both claims are accurate. Neither says the proposition is false. 'Whether (ii) => (i) holds with J+-only openness is not settled' is correct. stronglyCausalOpen_of_alexandrovTopology_eq (CausallyOpen -> alexandrovTopology = inst -> StronglyCausalOpen) is what DEC-8 closes the proposition with. A remark for the master: OQ-69's parenthetical ('That decides whether DEC-8's +/- is needed') holds only for a 'no'. A 'yes' leaves that question open, as the REPORT states, and OQ-9 is RULED by DEC-8.
